title: The Impossible Postcard
premise: Bram Winterbourne, a wedding planner whose own engagement ended in scandal and memory loss after an accident, has spent three years hiding inside other people's perfect days. To survive her family's reunion at the Brightwater estate, she hires Theo Marsh, a quiet archivist restoring the town's historical postcards—including one impossible card that seems to depict Bram herself on a day she cannot remember. As their fake romance turns real, Bram uncovers evidence that her family falsified the accident's story to protect its reputation, forcing her to choose between reclaiming her erased identity and preserving the career built on forgetting. In the end, she publicly tells the truth at her sister's wedding, loses the family firm but gains herself, and chooses Theo with a postcard sent from nowhere she's ever been.
about_author: F. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former estate archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's love letters before turning to fiction. They write romances about people who mistake safety for happiness.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. She orchestrates a flawless society wedding while privately flinching at every vow, revealing her rule: plan love, never feel it. A call from her mother summons her to the family reunion at Brightwater House—and demands she bring a partner she doesn't have. Emotional beat: polished control cracking into dread.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Hunting a plus-one, she finds Theo Marsh cataloguing postcards in the town archive, including one showing a woman in a yellow dress at Brightwater House—a woman wearing Bram's face, dated three days before her accident. She hires him impulsively. Emotional beat: curiosity overriding caution; first spark of being seen.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Lie
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He studies his new client and realizes her 'facts' don't match the archive records he's read. At a rehearsal dinner for the reunion weekend, they perform couplehood so convincingly it unsettles them both. Emotional beat: the fake beginning to feel dangerously easy.

chapters.title: Yellow Dress
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. At the reunion, relatives recount the accident differently than Bram remembers—or fails to remember. Her aunt goes pale at the mention of the postcard. By dessert, Bram and Theo's staged closeness has become real enough to scare her. Emotional beat: memory as a locked room someone else holds the key to.

chapters.title: What the Family Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Digging into estate papers, Theo finds letters suggesting Bram's fiancé ended things weeks before the 'accident,' and that her family reshaped the story to protect a business merger. He hesitates—telling her could destroy the fragile trust they've built. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth.

chapters.title: The Version of Me That Stayed
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Confronting her mother, Bram learns she herself agreed to forget—to accept the family's version in exchange for the firm and a painless life. The revelation gutters her sense of identity. She runs to Theo, and they cross from pretend to real. Emotional beat: grief and relief entangled.

chapters.title: Terms of the Merger
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Bram's mother offers Theo money to disappear before he can publish or testify, revealing how deep the corruption runs—and threatening his archive position. Meanwhile the firm moves to sever Bram. Emotional beat: power tightening its grip; stakes turn professional as well as personal.

chapters.title: Running Out of Summer
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. With her sister's wedding days away—the event Bram is contracted to plan—she must decide whether to speak the truth and torch her career, or stay silent and keep the life that was bought with her memory. Theo refuses to choose for her. Emotional beat: the cost of every option made visible.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the wedding, mid-toast, Bram abandons her script and tells the assembled guests what the family buried. The room fractures; her mother disowns the story and half the guests; the firm's biggest client walks out. But her sister takes her hand, and Theo stands when no one else does. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken at the altar of appearances.

chapters.title: Postmarked Nowhere
chapters.summary: Bram's POV, months later. Stripped of the family firm, Bram builds a small honest planning practice of her own. Theo publishes the archive findings; the impossible postcard turns out to be a photo of Bram on the happy day she chose to forget—now remembered. She mails him a postcard from a town she's never visited: 'Come find me.' He does. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed, love chosen freely.
